clue.text: PM fully extended dealing with dying cause

definitions.note: adjectival use, as in a post-mortem report

blocks.note: first meaning: the abbreviation PM written out in full
second meaning: concerned with establishing why someone died

explanation.surface: A prime minister drags things out while handling a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but here it is the medical abbreviation, which spelt out is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem examination is carried out to determine the cause of a person's death.

clue.text: Individual entered theatre a long time ago

definitions.note: adverbial phrase for a noun naming a remote period

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it, so the first word ends up enclosed

blocks.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
an individual is one person

explanation.surface: Someone recalls joining the theatre many years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' stands for the acting profession, as in 'going on the stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era, used loosely for any very distant past time.

clue.text: Artist establishes gambling location on outskirts of Izmir

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: Reno in Nevada is a famous gambling city
the two end letters of the Turkish city

explanation.surface: A painter sets up a casino just outside a Turkish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was the French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Visit old city that's somewhat grim

blocks.note: to do a place is to visit it as a tourist
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A tourist tours an ancient city that turns out rather bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' looks like a signal to take part of a word, but it simply softens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern and gloomy in manner, a milder kind of grim.

clue.text: One recruited in spring to oversee servers

definitions.note: describes the role rather than naming the person

indicators.note: someone recruited in joins from outside and ends up within the group

blocks.note: a headwater is the spring or source of a river
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is hired one spring to supervise the serving staff.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into HEADWATER after its A: HEADWA-I-TER. 'Spring' looks like a season but is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A head waiter is the senior waiter in a restaurant who supervises the other waiting staff.

clue.text: Feel a git when drifting? Find something meaningful to do

indicators.note: drifting letters wander out of their positions and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone drifting aimlessly feels foolish and is told to find a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: A git is British slang for a contemptible or foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'get a life' is a retort urging someone to stop wasting time and do something worthwhile.

clue.text: Series of notes Tudor emissary kept hidden

indicators.note: what is kept hidden lies concealed within the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A Tudor envoy kept a set of secret letters concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Do, re, mi are the first three notes of the sol-fa scale, a series of musical notes.

clue.text: Peel initially rejected Irish nationalist demands

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Robert Peel at first turned down what Irish nationalists demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel looks like the 19th-century British prime minister Robert Peel, who dealt with Irish questions, but it is the skin of a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel and rind are both the outer skin of a fruit.

clue.text: Travelling men hove to at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Sailors on a voyage bring their ship to a stop on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hove to' is a nautical term for bringing a ship to a halt, which fits the seafaring picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the move is in transit, going from place to place.

clue.text: Supremo jittery, hiding display of feeling

indicators.note: the words are hiding something concealed within their letters

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A nervous boss conceals any outward sign of emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoji is a small digital icon used in messages to show an emotion.

clue.text: It's OK for Americans to call out these two figures

blocks.note: first meaning: American radio slang for message received, okay
second meaning: two numbers said one after the other

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the ten-codes of US police and CB radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten-four is the US radio code meaning affirmative, understood.

clue.text: Doctor added essence of phenol — it got nowhere

definitions.note: a clause describing what the answer, a noun, is

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the two middle letters of the chemical

explanation.surface: A chemist adds phenol to an experiment that goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person but is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a road or line of enquiry that leads nowhere.

clue.text: Happy working atmosphere

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: An office with a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'walking on air', being elated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on air, as in walking on air, is to be elated and joyful.

clue.text: Gardening equipment, if lost, would be more concerning

indicators.note: if a word lost from the answer leaves another word, the lost word must have sat inside it

blocks.note: more frightening, more worrying
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tool which, if it went missing, would be worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: it describes what remains once a word is lost from the answer, so that word must sit inside the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarifier is a garden tool that rakes moss and thatch out of a lawn.

clue.text: What rude customer in diner may give and get

definitions.text: What rude customer in diner may give and get

blocks.clueFragment: What rude customer in diner may give
blocks.note: surface reading: a curt, abrupt command barked at the staff
setter's reading: a quickly cooked dish of the kind a diner serves

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both a brusque instruction and fast food cooked to order, so the rude diner issues one and is served the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In US diners, short-order cooking means simple dishes prepared quickly; a short order is also a curt command.

clue.text: Embarrassed by horse going astray — it's a distraction

blocks.note: red in the face with embarrassment
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified when their horse wanders off, which draws attention away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going astray' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym. Horse for heroin, and so H, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that diverts attention from what matters.

clue.text: The rich live off these obese people from the country

definitions.note: plural pronoun standing for a singular idiom

blocks.note: the fat, as a collective noun for overweight people
of the land means coming from the countryside

explanation.surface: A jibe that wealthy people grow fat on overweight country folk.
explanation.definitionFit: To live off the fat of the land is an idiom for living in luxury on the best of everything.

clue.text: Sadly, great philosopher's got no time for Russia's neighbours

indicators.note: having got none of something means it has been taken away from the word

blocks.note: alas is a cry of sorrow
Immanuel Kant, the German philosopher, with the possessive s
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A lament that a famous thinker had no time for the Russians' neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: T is removed from KANTS. Alaska lies across the Bering Strait from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaskans live in the US state separated from Russia only by the narrow Bering Strait.

clue.text: Spray creates a moister distribution

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters are redistributed

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A spray gives a damper, more even coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine spray.

clue.text: Spooner kept stuff from angry milliner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

blocks.note: had means kept or possessed
matter is stuff, material
the two words said together, with their opening sounds then traded

explanation.surface: Spooner holds onto some goods taken from a furious hat-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of HAD MATTER gives MAD HATTER, the character in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A mad hatter is literally an angry maker of hats, and the Hatter is Lewis Carroll's tea-party host.

clue.text: Pair swapping academy for university is definitely on

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means a letter is taken out and a different one put in its place

blocks.note: a double is a pair
A is a standard abbreviation for academy
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A couple trading an academy place for a university one is certainly going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In DOUBLE, U gives way to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doable can be achieved, and 'it's on' in casual speech means it can and will happen.

clue.text: Singular shape causes dispute about what it should be called

definitions.text: causes dispute about what it should be called
definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, a noun

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a cone is a solid geometric shape

explanation.surface: An unusual form sparks argument over its proper name.
explanation.walkthrough: A scone is a small British baked cake; Britons argue whether it rhymes with 'gone' or 'stone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scone is notorious in Britain for the debate over how its name should be pronounced.

clue.text: Central fund gets involved in cut — that's really bright

indicators.note: central points to the middle of the word, so only its core letters are kept
becoming involved in something means going inside it

blocks.note: a slit is a narrow cut
the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A core budget gets caught up in spending cuts, which is a brilliant outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' reads as an adjective for the fund, but it picks the word's middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlit means lit by the sun, so brightly illuminated.

clue.text: One following second speaker

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a talker is someone who speaks

explanation.surface: Someone who comes after the first speaker at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One following second speaker' reads as a debating order of speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is a person who obsessively follows someone.

clue.text: Almost declare figure immediately

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word's final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to state is to declare

explanation.surface: Someone nearly announces a number at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes meet: STATE loses its last letter, a stat is a statistic, and stat is medical shorthand for at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is short for statistic, a numerical figure, and from Latin statim it is hospital jargon for without delay.

clue.text: Increasingly weird Labour leader heard going after family

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by the sound of the name rather than its spelling

blocks.note: kin are family members
Keir Starmer, leader of the UK Labour Party, his first name respelt to match its sound

explanation.surface: A political leader is said to be getting stranger after a family scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' places the leader's name after KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkier is the comparative of kinky, meaning eccentric or odd, so more and more weird.

clue.text: Excitement can be free after a trip?

definitions.text: can be free after a trip
definitions.note: describes the answer rather than replacing it

blocks.note: first meaning: a thrill

blocks.clueFragment: can be free after a trip
blocks.note: second meaning: in football a free one is awarded after a player is tripped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' and 'free' suggest a holiday or drugs, but this is football: a foul such as tripping earns a free kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick is slang for a thrill, and a free kick is the football restart awarded for a foul.

clue.text: Everyone is on board to make major bet

definitions.note: verb phrase for an adverbial answer, as in going all in

blocks.note: first meaning: everybody has been included or has joined
second meaning: in poker, staking all of one's chips

explanation.walkthrough: The poker sense is 'going all in', betting every chip at once.
explanation.definitionFit: All in means everyone is included, and in poker it means staking one's entire stack.

clue.text: Geometric theory eccentric uncle maintains

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are knocked out of order
to maintain is to hold, so one part is kept inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a theory is an idea

explanation.surface: An odd relative clings to a pet mathematical theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled uncle splits around the theory, four letters before and one after.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclidean geometry is the classical geometry set out by the Greek mathematician Euclid.
